mechanism_narrative: As residential mobility continues its recent decline, it signals a shift in population behavior towards spending less time at home and more time engaging in out-of-home activities, directly boosting retail and recreation visits over the next two weeks.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continuing their upward trends.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent upward trend across multiple mobility categories suggests an ongoing easing of public health restrictions, which will continue to directly permit and encourage increased retail and recreation activity, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 7 days, despite PARKS mobility rising by more than 2 points week-on-week.

failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility continues its upward trend, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A continued strong recovery in WORKPLACES mobility, driven by businesses reopening, will directly increase foot traffic in commercial areas during weekdays, leading to a significant uplift in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks, provided no new lockdowns are imposed.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES mobility continues to rise week-on-week
